version.changelog: Security: remove bare --token arg. Credentials only via --token-file, --token-stdin, or NOTION_API_KEY env var. Never exposed in process listings or shell history.

llm.summary: The skill appears to implement a legitimate Notion sync CLI, but registry metadata omits the required Notion credential and there are a few minor surprises (local state file, token-from-stdin behavior) that you should understand before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill's code and SKILL.md clearly require a Notion integration token (supports --token-file, --token-stdin, or NOTION_API_KEY), but the registry metadata lists no required environment variables or primary credential. Requesting a Notion token is appropriate for the stated purpose, however the published metadata is inconsistent/omitted and should have declared NOTION_API_KEY or a primary credential.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions and scripts stay within the declared purpose: they read local markdown files, call api.notion.com, convert/append blocks, query databases, and monitor pages. Scripts also read/write a workspace-local state file (memory/notion-watch-state.json). They do not call unknown external endpoints or attempt to read unrelated system config. Note: token can be read from stdin (fd 0), a token file, or env var — reading stdin may block if misused.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec — this is instruction- and script-based. All code is included in the skill bundle and nothing is downloaded or extracted at install time, minimizing install-time supply-chain risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The code legitimately needs a Notion API token and supports NOTION_API_KEY, token files, or stdin. However the registry metadata does not declare any required env var or primary credential. No other credentials or unrelated env variables are accessed. The omission in metadata is the primary proportionality problem (it under-declares the secret access this skill requires).
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (no forced inclusion). The scripts create and update a local state file at memory/notion-watch-state.json in the working directory when using watch-notion.js — this is reasonable for a watcher but worth noting because it creates persistent state in the user's workspace. The skill does not request system-wide privileges or modify other skills.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill's behavior mostly matches its Notion sync purpose, but the registry metadata failed to declare that a Notion API token is required. Before installing: 1) Treat this as code that will have your Notion integration token. Create a dedicated integration token with minimal scopes and share only the pages/databases you want the integration to access. 2) Prefer providing the token via a token file (the skill recommends this) or stdin rather than embedding it on the command line. 3) Be aware watch-notion.js writes memory/notion-watch-state.json in your current workspace — run it in a workspace where writing that file is acceptable. 4) Verify the source (the GitHub repo) and, if possible, inspect the included scripts yourself or run them in an isolated/test environment first (e.g., a disposable Notion integration and a test workspace). 5) Ask the publisher/registry to update the skill metadata to declare NOTION_API_KEY (or the primary credential) so the required permissions are explicit. If you need help checking token scopes or running the scripts safely, consider running the provided test script (scripts/test-normalize.js) in a sandbox first.
